When Abraham rises to sapad for Sarah in Genesis 23:2, the word carries the weight of audible, public grief — not private sorrow. Zechariah 12:10 envisions a future day when all Jerusalem will sapad as for an only son, a passage that gave rise to rich messianic interpretation."
